clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock moved from 8:13 p.m. to 8:14 p.m., a net shift of 0.2 minutes. The advance was limited because courts and some members of Congress still imposed checks, but the week's strongest actions were structural and favored further concentration of power.

grand_total_points.note: The weekly net change was modest but real because structural executive gains outweighed partial judicial and legislative resistance.

delta_summary.moral_floor: The moral floor continued to erode unevenly: formal legality persisted in many settings, but stewardship, restraint, and good faith weakened as institutions grew more contingent on political favor.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: This was a week of consolidation rather than spectacle, with legal protection, electoral restriction, symbolic control, and donor influence reinforcing one another.

traits_moved.note: Nineteen tracked traits worsened, with the sharpest movement in voter suppression, religion as state legitimacy, rewritten national history, and law as executive weapon.

long_synopsis: Week 70 brought a small but meaningful move forward on the Democracy Clock as executive power was arranged to protect allies, shape elections, and claim public symbolism. The Justice Department created a $1.776 billion Anti-Weaponization Fund while extending tax-related protection to Trump, his family, and affiliated companies, joining public money to legal immunity. The Supreme Court weakened Voting Rights Act protections, and state officials in South Carolina and North Carolina moved quickly on redistricting and election rules that critics said would dilute or suppress Black voting power. The administration also redirected America250 planning into Freedom 250 and staged Christian nationalist public ceremony while advancing leader-centered monuments and donor access. Courts, some lawmakers, and civil society pushed back, especially on records, immigration tactics, and oversight. But most resistance was reactive, narrow, and slower than the structural changes underway.
short_synopsis: Week 70 moved the clock slightly forward as the administration fused legal protection, public money, voting-rights rollback, and symbolic glorification into a broader pattern of personal rule. Courts and some lawmakers resisted, but mostly after the ground had already shifted.
